title: Segatt Tools — escolha o mundo visual
question: O sorteio escolheu Console Manual. Fique com ele, pegue uma alternativa ou sorteie de novo.

options.label: Console Manual
options.lineage: 1990s Japanese console game manuals and arcade instruction cards
options.thesis: Every tweak explained like a game manual page: numbered, color-coded, impossible to misread.
options.viewport: Tweaks: left rail, four sections coded with the four face-button colors, each row a live-state toggle with a numbered callout and a mono 'what changes' line.
options.risk: Turns toy-like if the four colors leave the category chips; it has to hold Apple-grade restraint.

raised.raise: From Labanotation: the task log draws each run as a bar whose length is its real duration.
From the Crouwel grid: every element snaps to one 4px module; no off-grid value anywhere.
From the lexicon: risky tweaks earn more apparatus (warning, detail, revert note), never bigger type.
From the variable-font specimen: one preset control remaps the whole list live, with a running count readout.

options.label: Desk Instrument
options.lineage: Dieter Rams' Braun appliances and Teenage Engineering devices
options.thesis: The app as a precise desk object: charcoal body, one orange control, status as small lit dots.
options.viewport: Tweaks as a calm dense list on a dot-grid ground; a lit dot shows each tweak's real state; orange marks only the primary action.
options.risk: Familiar: enthusiast and Apple-adjacent design culture, and many tools already borrow this look.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Windows' own typographic heritage: live tiles for health, giant lowercase section names.
options.viewport: Dashboard of live tiles (tweaks applied, updates pending, space freed) with pivot headers for each tweak category.
options.case: Wins audience identification (Windows users know it by heart); loses clarity where cropped type hides labels.
options.risk: Reads as a 2012 Windows throwback; Apple-grade finish is hard to reach in flat tiles.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Every change is a coupon: applied, reverted and failed stamp themselves; nothing silently disappears.
options.viewport: Tweaks as coupon rows with stamped states and a history column of every applied and reverted change.
options.case: Wins product clarity (reversible, honest history); loses audience identification for gamers.
options.risk: A paper-and-travel world can feel foreign in a gaming tool.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Time as a vertical staff where length is exact duration.
options.viewport: Task history as a vertical staff of duration blocks.
options.case: Loses both axes: gamers do not read dance scores, and a staff hides the toggle list.
options.kept: Length encodes real duration in the task log.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid as the armature of every screen.
options.viewport: Sections on a visible cell grid with monumental grid-built titles.
options.case: Loses both axes: poster typography fights a dense working list.
options.kept: One strict module that every element snaps to.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Entries ranked by apparatus, guide words naming the span in view.
options.viewport: Tweaks as dictionary entries in a fixed measure with guide words at the head.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish for gamers, and cream paper is a known AI default.
options.kept: Rank by apparatus, not by size.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: One slider remaps the whole page live with a readout.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with an axis slider driving a glyph grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: the subject is type, not the PC.
options.kept: One control remaps the whole list live, with a count readout.
options.risk: A type toy, not a tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Windows 11 Settings-style app, executed flawlessly.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, page title, cards of toggles grouped by category.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Windows Settings and WinUtil by design.
